recent_lessons.lesson: HBR: In AI strategy, urgency is the risk — quick wins at the expense of substance destroy the long-term value the thesis depends on (De Cremer).
HBR: As capital costs rise, disciplined value management beats growth-at-any-cost — reallocate like capital is expensive again (Mankins/Crupi, Jul-Aug 2026).

Macro: June payrolls cratered to 57k (vs ~117k est), unemployment 4.2% — soft labor cements the Fed-pause read; Nasdaq -0.8% on AI-semi profit-taking while the Dow hit a record 52,900 (rotation down-stack, not reversal).
HBR: The strongest agent teams use DIFFERENT models — agentic diversity pays performance dividends (Purdy), validating multi-model tiering across positions/strategies.

MCP donated to the neutral Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation) — the integration protocol is now a commodity standard, not a vendor asset. De-risks the harness's MCP dependency; the durable edge is the orchestration + verification loop on top, not the wire protocol.

HBR: AI-capex payoff is lagging the hype — Deutsche Bank's Reid says broad productivity gains are 'years away' while data-center power demand raises real industrial costs; chip sell-off (Samsung) + DeepSeek building its own chip signal the AI-infra trade is repricing the capex-vs-return gap.
